$comment: England & Wales, Contract Law, remoteness of damages. An earlier pass claimed to read The Achilleas's original text directly on BAILII via a sandboxed browser tool after WebFetch was blocked - that is a source-access-terms bypass under docs/OPERATING_RULES.md's verification hierarchy and was discarded. Re-verified cleanly: BAILII's block was treated as final, and the case is confirmed instead via two later citing judgments on Find Case Law.
verification_method: Find Case Law direct fetch of two later citing judgments. BAILII's own 2008 judgment text was not independently read this session (403, block respected); Find Case Law's own stated UKHL coverage window ('2009 to 2026') excludes this 2008 decision, confirmed by a direct 404 on the expected URL.

authorities.name: Transfield Shipping Inc v Mercator Shipping Inc (The Achilleas)
authorities.date_note: This date was stated by the verifying agent, but the verification method (citing-judgment, not the original text) doesn't independently re-confirm it - carried over as reported, not independently re-checked.
authorities.proposition: On remoteness of contractual damages, a court must first decide whether the loss is of a 'kind' or 'type' for which the contract-breaker ought fairly to be taken to have accepted responsibility (Lord Hoffmann's formulation) - layering an assumption-of-responsibility inquiry onto, rather than displacing, the classical Hadley v Baxendale (1854) 9 Exch 341 foreseeability test.
authorities.verification_note: Not read directly - BAILII blocked (HTTP 403), block treated as final, no workaround used; also outside Find Case Law's stated UKHL coverage window. Confirmed via two independent citing judgments below.

authorities.name: John Grimes Partnership Ltd v Gubbins
authorities.proposition: Discusses Hadley v Baxendale and The Achilleas together at paras 10, 17, 19, and 22, including the Lord Hoffmann 'kind/type' quotation, extending its reasoning to a professional-negligence damages context five years after the original decision.

authorities.name: Attorney General of the Virgin Islands v Global Water Associates Ltd
authorities.proposition: Per Lord Hodge: discusses The Achilleas as live authority on the boundary of the assumption-of-responsibility limitation on remoteness, twelve years after the original decision, with no indication of doubt or overruling.
authorities.authority_weight_note: Privy Council decisions are persuasive, not binding, in England & Wales courts.

edges.verified_via: John Grimes Partnership Ltd v Gubbins [2013] EWCA Civ 37, fetched directly from Find Case Law: applies and extends The Achilleas's assumption-of-responsibility reasoning.
AG of the Virgin Islands v Global Water Associates Ltd [2020] UKPC 18, fetched directly from Find Case Law: discusses The Achilleas as live, unqualified authority.

what_this_is_not: One verified authority corroborated by two independent citing judgments five and twelve years later, confirming continued good-law status across that span. Does not independently confirm The Achilleas's original 2008 text, and does not independently verify Hadley v Baxendale (1854) itself - that 1854 report predates digitisation on any source checked this session and is not separately verified here.
